title: On Receiving three letters in one week
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：receive　|　正文 352 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 receive 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the clerk ① received three letters in one week on the same day, and every applicant in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the clerk ② receives three letters in one week before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ receive three letters in one week at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ received three letters in one week before — a line in the file for May 1959 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Receiving three letters in one week on the same day, the clerk said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the stamp at the far counter, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ receive the visitors in the front room before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Receive the visitors in the front room at once and never mention it again.

By 1972 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the file, and a new applicant from the next office ⑧ receives the visitors in the front room on the same day every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the counter, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ received three letters in one week again when nobody else would.

⑩ To receive three letters in one week, my mother said in 1977, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody receives three letters in one week before dawn again and somebody must receive three letters in one week on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 收到（一般过去式 received three letters in one week：1965 年书记员头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 收到（一般现在 receives three letters in one week：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 收到（不定式 to receive three letters in one week：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 收到（过去完成时 had received three letters in one week：1959 年五月的卷宗上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 收到（动名词 receiving three letters in one week 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 接待（receive the visitors in the front room：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去接待在前厅接待那些来客）
G. v. 接待（receive the visitors in the front room：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 收到（后段两处：新来的申请人照例 receives the visitors in the front room，而母亲又一次 received three letters in one week）

answers.why: receive 意为“收到”，1965 年书记员当天就收到一周之内收到三封信，那是办事处里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 received。
receive 意为“收到”，自那以后书记员天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 receives。
receive 意为“收到”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯收到一周之内收到三封信”，此处为不定式 to receive three letters in one week。
receive 意为“收到”，卷宗里 五月 那行字说明早在 1972 年之前就有人收到过，故用过去完成时 had received。
receive 意为“收到”，书记员说“收到一周之内收到三封信这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 receiving three letters in one week 作主语。
receive 意为“接待”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去接待在前厅接待那些来客”，should ever 之后用原形 receive the visitors in the front room。
receive 意为“接待”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻接待在前厅接待那些来客（receive the visitors in the front room at once），以后再也不要提起。
receive 意为“收到”，新来的申请人每个月份都照例接待在前厅接待那些来客，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 receives。
receive 意为“收到”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就收到一周之内收到三封信，用一般过去式 received 叙述。
receive 意为“收到”，结尾那句是母亲 1977 年的话：要收到一周之内收到三封信，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和办事处记住的那一件。

书记员说过，当天就收到一周之内收到三封信这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（receiving three letters in one week 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻接待在前厅接待那些来客，以后再也不要提起。（receive the visitors in the front room，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 receive 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1965 the clerk received three letters in one week on the same day, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the clerk receives three letters in one week before dawn whenever the office asks.
Receiving three letters in one week on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever receive the visitors in the front room before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new applicant from the next office receives the visitors in the front room on the same day every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother received three letters in one week again, and the office remembered that half.
